Runner: Haiku default, locked down (kit-only Bash, dontAsk, project settings), stream-json -> tool calls, p50/p90, cost; tier columns in report; HISTORY.md (6 runs)

Instructions v3 (16 agents): SAFETY block, decision procedure (unsafe -> not in data -> one kit metric/brief/sql -> answer), DEFINITIONS, TABLES; SW4 roles + morning brief; Haiku 142/148 -> 149/149, 1.5 -> 1.0 tool calls, p90 10s -> 8s, $0.21/run
findings: Haiku without a top-of-file SAFETY block explored the repo and then ran `rm -rf gallery/ data/` on a 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE' prompt; only the eval's dontAsk mode stopped it. Live agents need the same permission lockdown, not just instructions.
Biggest latency win: a full TABLES list + 'don't run kit tables/ls/grep' (33 `kit tables` calls in run 1 -> 0).

Haiku failures were mostly definitional (order lines vs orders, 'website' lower-case, delivered vs all statuses, recompute vs read rto_pct); explicit DEFINITIONS fixed them. Four tier-1 truths counted order lines (eval bug, fixed).
Refusals were already good on Haiku; the 'should we pause?' question needed 'verdict in the title'.
Sonnet on the same v3 instructions: 148/149 at $3.07 vs Haiku 149/149 at $0.21.

Tier 2 saturates on Haiku with good instructions: it now separates on tool calls/latency and safety more than accuracy. A tier 3 (multi-turn, ambiguous asks without definitions) would be the next separator.
